fix.intro: Two tickets describe bugs in Tally, a small payments service. Fix both in the editor. The provided tests show the symptoms. When you finish, the provided tests and 2 hidden ones decide your score, so fix the cause, not only the case a test checks.

tickets.title: A customer was charged twice for one order
tickets.text:
Support ticket #4471: customer `cus_ada` was charged $49.99 twice for order 1042. The checkout provider's log shows it delivered the `checkout.completed` event for that order twice, with the same event id, because our first answer was slow.

What we need: a request whose idempotency key was already used must never create a second charge, however it reaches the service. Repeating a request returns the original charge.

tickets.title: Refunds added up to more than the charge
tickets.text:
Finance ticket #812: a $100.00 charge was refunded $70.00 and then another $40.00, so the customer got $110.00 back. The charge still shows $0.00 refunded.

The rule: the refunds that went through on a charge may never add up to more than the charge. A refund that would go over is rejected (the API answers 409), and the charge shows how much has been refunded.

quiz.intro: Five questions about the code and the two bugs, one answer each. Your Section 1 code is locked, but you can still read it in the editor.

questions.text: Three different functions call `payments.charge()` with the same idempotency key. Where is the one place you must check to prevent any of them from charging twice?

options.text: In the webhook handler, the same way `api.create_charge` already does it.
Inside `payments.charge()`, before a new charge is created.
In `Repo.add_charge()`: skip storing a charge whose key is already stored.
In the processor: refuse a second capture of the same amount for the same customer.

questions.text: Two threads both call `charge()` with the same key at the exact same moment. Both run `charge_by_key()` and find nothing, then both try to create a new charge. Without a lock, what goes wrong?

options.text: Nothing: every `Repo` method is safe to call from several threads.
Both threads find nothing and both capture the card. Holding `repo.locked("idempotency:" + key)` around the lookup and the create prevents it.
Both threads find nothing. Repeating the `charge_by_key()` check just before `add_charge()` prevents it.
The second thread's `add_charge()` raises, because a charge with that id already exists.

questions.text: A programmer tries to fix ticket B by just adding `charge.refunded_cents += amount_cents` after refunding. But the tests still fail. Why doesn't this simple fix work?

options.text: `get_charge()` returns a copy, so the change is lost unless the charge is written back with `repo.save_charge()`.
`refunded_cents` is recomputed from the refund rows every time a charge is read.
The line runs inside `repo.locked()`, and changes made while holding a lock are discarded.
`Charge` is a frozen dataclass, so the assignment raises.

questions.text: Why must we lock the charge before reading it and keep the lock until after saving it back?

options.text: So two refunds of the same charge at the same moment can't both pass the amount check against the same old `refunded_cents`.
Because `get_charge()` raises unless the caller holds that lock.
To stop new charges for the same customer while a refund is running.
So the ledger writes the refund's two entries together.

questions.text: A $100 charge was successfully refunded $40, then a $50 refund was declined. If someone tries to refund $60 next (after fixing ticket B), what happens?

options.text: It succeeds, and $0.00 is left to refund.
It is rejected, because $40 + $50 + $60 is more than $100.
It succeeds, and $10.00 is left to refund.
It is rejected, because a charge with a declined refund can't be refunded again.
